# Adhd

This folder catalogs the six core pharmacological treatments for ADHD tracked within the Danish national ADHD database quality monitoring system. Each page details a specific medication—ranging from stimulants like methylphenidate and dexamfetamine to non-stimulants like atomoxetine and guanfacine—and documents its inclusion in national clinical quality indicators such as Indikator 6 for children and Indikator 11 for adults. The entries synthesize how these substances are used to measure treatment coverage, evaluate regional variations, and guide evidence-based practice across Danish healthcare regions.

## Pages

- [[atomoxetin-n06ba09|Atomoxetin (N06BA09)]] — A non-stimulant norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor tracked in both pediatric and adult national quality indicators for pharmacological treatment coverage.
- [[dexamfetamin-n06ba02|Dexamfetamin (N06BA02)]] — A stimulant medication monitored to evaluate the systemic balance of pharmacological interventions across different Danish regions.
- [[guanfacin-c02ac02|Guanfacin (C02AC02)]] — A secondary treatment option for patients with comorbidities, integrated into national metrics to capture the full spectrum of medical interventions.
- [[lisdexamfetamin-n06ba12|Lisdexamfetamin (N06BA12)]] — A prodrug of dexamfetamine with extended duration, serving as a key metric in the political steering and clinical quality development of ADHD care.
- [[methylphenidat-n06ba04|Methylphenidat (N06BA04)]] — The most common pharmacological treatment for ADHD in Denmark, heavily monitored for regional implementation strengths and coverage.
- [[modafinil-n06ba07|Modafinil (N06BA07)]] — An alternative treatment under specific clinical conditions, included in national indicators to ensure comprehensive tracking of all prescribed ADHD medications.
